standard_prerequisites.name: The G-ring condition, meaning that the formal fibres of the local rings are geometrically regular
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: defined in the same section, source lines 12179-12261

standard_prerequisites.name: Complete Noetherian local rings have regular formal fibres

standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the completion of the completion regular.

standard_prerequisites.name: Regularity of ring maps composes, and regularity of a map can be tested after factoring through an intermediate ring

standard_prerequisites.use: Carries the regularity from the corner rings back to the local map at the chosen prime.

core_obligations: Assume the maps from the localisations at maximal ideals to their completions are regular and pick a prime p together with a maximal ideal containing it (proof lines 12398-12403).
Choose a prime of the completion lying over the localisation of p and display the commutative square of the four rings (proof lines 12403-12407).

Use the hypothesis, the proposition on complete Noetherian rings and the regularity of localisations to see that the composite from the localisation at the maximal ideal to the completion of the completion is regular (proof lines 12407-12416).
Factor that map through the localisation at p and apply the permanence statement to conclude that the formal fibres at p are regular, hence that the ring is a G-ring (proof lines 12416-12426).
proof_roadmap: Set up the prime and the maximal ideal containing it (proof lines 12398-12403).
Build the commutative square of rings (proof lines 12403-12407).
Transfer regularity around the square (proof lines 12407-12416).
Factor through the localisation and apply permanence (proof lines 12416-12427).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a Noetherian ring it suffices to test geometric regularity of the formal fibres of the localisations at maximal ideals, and the proof is a 30-line diagram chase. Starting from a prime, it chooses a maximal ideal containing it and a prime of the completion lying over the localised prime, displays the commutative square of four rings, and then transfers regularity corner by corner: the completion map is regular by hypothesis, the completion of the completion is regular by the proposition on complete Noetherian G-rings, the localisation is regular because localisations are, and regularity composes and factors through the intermediate localisation, so the permanence statement gives regularity for the local ring at the original prime. Each corner of the square is used at a precisely identified step.
